doc.title: Phil Mead interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 1, 2006

title: The drummers: Wormworth, Zito and Grogan
summary: Jimmy Wormworth's bop drumming and later career, plus the remarkable drummers who drove the band.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: And from a very musical family too, with Tori who went on with Tony Bennett and all that.

So then the other guy who mostly played with us was Jimmy Wormworth, and he’s sort of the guy who I think of as our drummer because Jimmy and I became very close friends. But Jimmy was my age so he was 18 starting out and he was a bop drummer. Ronnie was always a big band drummer. I mean he could play anything but he was a big band, swing band drummer. But Jimmy was a bop drummer, a wonderful drummer. And he and I became very close friends and stay in touch to this day. And he of course was the drummer for Lambert, Hendricks and Ross, played with almost everybody in the fifties and sixties and just had a remarkable career and is still playing now with Charles Davis and still, I heard him a couple of years ago when they came up to Vermont and he hadn’t lost a beat. He’s wonderful. So those were two. And then occasionally when the two of them couldn’t make it there was a guy whose nickname was Grogan and I’m trying to come back with his name, but he was a marvelous drummer. So we had these just killer drummers. And I think they really kicked the band along. And I think everybody in the

band was a pretty good musician but the drummers were certainly spectacular. I don’t think there was any other college band then or now that had this kind of talent just week in and week out just kicking you along. And so I think that had a lot to do with the excitement at the beginning and of course once we got playing then it just all kind of came together.
